summary.name: South Bay SRE Meetup - Netflix Cloud Performance Team
summary.one_liner: A 2017 YouTube talk by Netflix's Cloud Performance Team on how they measure real-user streaming performance across devices and ISPs, presented at the South Bay SRE Meetup.
use_cases: Learning how Netflix measures real-user performance
Reviewing approaches to device and ISP segmentation in metrics
Studying anomaly detection for production performance data
Background on reducing metrics storage cost at scale
summary.what_it_does: The page is a YouTube video (2017, 33 likes, 2.7K views) of a South Bay SRE Meetup talk by the Netflix Cloud Performance Team. The chapter list covers topics such as building performance histograms, handling outliers with exponentially spaced buckets, collecting real user data, categorizing devices, data sketches, weighted averages, comparisons and filters, anomaly detection, and the cost and encoding of metrics at Netflix's scale. The page text contains only the chapter titles and related-video listings, so the specific claims made in the talk are not visible here.
notable: Covers Netflix's real-user performance measurement approach
Chapters on histograms, outliers, and data sketches
Discusses metrics cost savings and encoding at scale
caveats: Page text shows only chapter titles and metadata; talk content not visible
Video is from 2017 and may be dated
